subject: Post-call exec recap: Redwood for AuroraMed — exec summary & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: David Chen <david.chen@auroramed.com>, Rebecca Stone <rebecca.stone@auroramed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call exec recap: Redwood for AuroraMed — exec summary & next steps

Hi David / Rebecca —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick executive recap and proposed next steps so your team (and execs) can align on outcomes and risks. I’ve copied our AE manager (Aditya) and Solutions lead (Laura) for any procurement/legal questions.

Key pain points you shared:
- High latency and cost variability on current LLM endpoints when serving patient-facing summarization and coding assistance (esp. peak load during clinic hours).
- Data residency and auditability requirements for PHI-related inference (need audit logs and KMS integration).
- Need for predictable unit economics for budgeting across pilots and production.

Primary goals / success metrics:
- Reduce median 95th-percentile latency from ~450ms to <200ms for 512-token summaries.
- Achieve >40% reduction in per-token inference cost through batching, KV caching, and quantization profile without quality regressions.
- Meet AuroraMed security requirements: SOC 2 + KMS + VPC/private deployment for PHI workloads.

Risks called out:
- Procurement timeline (internal legal & security signoff) could push pilot from July to September if requirements aren’t pre-validated.
- Integration effort around data residency and on-prem connectors — we recommend a short technical spike ahead of procurement.

Procurement path & timeline (your proposed):
- Technical spike / pilot requirements doc: by 6/23 (AuroraMed engineering + Redwood SEs)
- Procurement review & budget decision: end of June / early July
- Pilot start (non-PHI sandbox): mid July

Immediate next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Redwood: send pricing deck and SOC2 evidence + short pilot scoping template (attached). (attached: redwood_pricing_deck_v2.pdf, soc2_evidence_stub.zip)
2) AuroraMed: confirm procurement contact and target budget window; share any required contract template or specific legal clauses to pre-check.
3) Schedule technical spike with AuroraMed engineering (30–60m) — suggested week of 6/22.
4) Set procurement call (legal + purchasing + IT security) — proposed 6/25.

Marissa — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite and include Laura/Aditya for any pricing/contract questions.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
(415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood_pricing_deck_v2.pdf (pricing deck, 12 slides), soc2_evidence_stub.zip (evidence index, redacted)

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call exec recap: Redwood for AuroraMed — exec summary & next steps

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear summary. High level confirmation from our side: this maps to what our CTO and Head of Product are looking for. A few clarifications / asks from the AuroraMed side:

- Procurement: Kevin Marshall (kevin.marshall@auroramed.com) is the purchasing lead — I’ve looped him into a separate thread and asked him to confirm budget range.
- Security: we need a short write-up on how audit logs are exposed and KMS key management works (customer-managed keys). SOC2 evidence looks fine at a glance — please share the encryption-at-rest and in-transit details.
- Timeline: we’re motivated to pilot in July, but legal/security review could extend this. If we can get the pilot scoping doc by 6/23 and a pricing/commitment option that allows a pilot-to-ELA conversion, that will greatly help internal approvals.

Proposed procurement call: I confirm 6/25 works for an initial cross-functional sync (Legal + Purchasing + IT Security). Please include Kevin and our legal rep if possible.

-David

David Chen

3) Procurement call: proposing Fri 6/25 at 10:00 AM PT. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda: intro, procurement questions, legal open items, and next steps.

Internal ask (Aditya / Laura): can you confirm standard discounting and whether a 12-month committed Dedicated plan can qualify for an introductory 20% discount? Also, Legal — are there any known non-starters in our standard SOW for a healthcare customer that requires on-prem/VPC controls?
